transcription.tex: \text{\textbf{Factor theorem}}\par\text{ \((x-p)\) is a factor of a polynomial f(x) if and only if f(p)=0.}
\text{\textbf{Example} For \(f(x)=x^3+x^2-4x-4\), test whether x−2 is a factor.}

\text{Alternatively compare coefficients: in (x−3)(ax²+bx+c), a=2, c=3 and b−3a=1 gives b=7. Try integer divisors of the constant term, or use a calculator table, to find a root.}

transcription.tex: \text{\textbf{Conjecture}}\par\text{ A mathematical statement not yet proved.}
\text{Goldbach’s conjecture: every even integer greater than 2 is a sum of two primes. Checking many cases supplies evidence, but does not prove every case.}
\text{\textbf{Theorem}}\par\text{ A mathematical statement that has been proved.}
\text{Fermat’s Last Theorem: for integers n>2 there are no positive integers a,b,c satisfying \(a^n+b^n=c^n\). Its proof was published in 1995.}

transcription.tex: \text{A proof states its assumptions, follows a logical sequence, covers every case and ends with a conclusion. Deduction starts with known facts.}
\text{\textbf{1} Prove that the product of two odd integers is odd.}
\text{Let p,q be integers. The odd integers have forms 2p+1 and 2q+1.\[(2p+1)(2q+1)=4pq+2p+2q+1\]\[=2(2pq+p+q)+1\]This is one more than an even integer, so the product is odd.}
\text{An identity holds for every permissible value: \(x(x-1)\equiv x^2-x\). By contrast, \(x^2=4\) holds only for x=±2.}

transcription.tex: \text{Prove that consecutive integer side lengths of a right-angled triangle must be 3,4,5.}
\text{\textbf{Insufficient argument}}\par\text{ Checking 3²+4²=5² shows one example works. It does not exclude other consecutive triples.}
\text{Let the positive integer sides be x,x+1,x+2. By Pythagoras,\[x^2+(x+1)^2=(x+2)^2\]\[x^2-2x-3=(x-3)(x+1)=0\]Since x>0, x=3. Therefore the sides must be 3,4,5.}
\text{Start from the given assumptions, rather than assuming the conclusion you are asked to prove.}

\text{\textbf{12} The equation \(kx^2+5kx+3=0\), where \(k\) is a constant, has no real roots. Prove that \(k\) satisfies the inequality \(0\le k<\frac{12}{25}\).  }

\text{\(kx^2+5kx+3=0\) has no real roots, so \(b^2-4ac<0\).\[\begin{aligned}(5k)^2-4k(3)&<0\\25k^2-12k&<0\\k(25k-12)&<0\\0<k&<\tfrac{12}{25}\end{aligned}\]When \(k=0\):\[(0)x^2+5(0)x+3=0,\qquad3=0\]which is impossible, so no real roots.}\par\text{ So combining these:\[0\le k<\tfrac{12}{25}\]}

transcription.tex: \text{\textbf{Proof by exhaustion}}\par\text{ Divide the possibilities into cases and prove each case.}
\text{\textbf{Disproof by counterexample}}\par\text{ One counterexample disproves a statement claiming every case works.}
\text{\textbf{1} Prove \(n^2+n\) is even for every integer n.}
\text{If n is even, n²+n is even+even, hence even. If n is odd, n²+n is odd+odd, hence even. These cover every integer, so the claim holds.}
\text{\textbf{2} Disprove: \(n^2-n+41\) is prime for every integer n.}
\text{\[n=41\Rightarrow n^2-n+41=41^2\]This is composite, so the claim is false.}

sourceMapping.method: Source-checked native text and LaTeX; explicit question/answer objects

transcription.tex: \text{\textbf{4} Prove each integer cube is a multiple of 9, or one more or one less.}
\text{Every integer is 3n,3n+1 or 3n+2.\[(3n)^3=9(3n^3)\]\[(3n+1)^3=9(3n^3+3n^2+n)+1\]\[(3n+2)^3=9(3n^3+6n^2+4n+1)-1\]The three cases give the required remainders.}
